html:
The conquest of Mecca was the entry of Muhammad's army into his birthplace in January 630, ending years of war with the quraysh.

The trigger was a breach of the truce signed at Hudaybiyyah. Muhammad led about 10,000 men from Medina toward Mecca. The Quraysh leader Abu Sufyan, seeing he could not win, gave up, and the city fell with little fighting. Muhammad granted a general amnesty to most of its people.

He cleared the idols out of the Kaaba and made it the central shrine of Islam. Many Meccan leaders became Muslims, and some of their families, including Abu Sufyan's son Muawiya, later gained high places in the new state. Within two years most of Arabia had joined. The prophet died in 632 and the community faced the question of his succession.
sum: The conquest of Mecca was the entry of Muhammad's army into his birthplace in January 630, ending years of war with the quraysh.
